plan.KONU:
•
Asking for and giving information
•
Talking about present events/situations
•
Talking about opportunities
I'm applying for...
Why do you want another degree?
Do many students in your country study abroad?
The number of people going abroad to study has been increasing year by year.
Can you give me some information about what facilities your hostel has?
There is an Internet connection and a bath in each room.
Could you talk about the advantages of one year exchange programme?
Your exchange programme is the best year of my life, because it is an opportunity to learn a new culture and a foreign language. I've been an ambassador of my native culture. In addition to this, I've made friends for a lifetime...
In what ways do volunteering programmes contribute to my future career?
They challenge you and provide an excellent framework for personal growth and development.
I want to apply for an exchange programme, but how?
You had better contact the related club in your area to learn about exchange opportunities, please.
Making the decision to live abroad for work or for study is a huge and life changing decision and you can have opportunities more than you have expected.
plan.KAZANIM:
Listening
•
Students will be able to complete a table according to the conversation about the orientation process of a course or school abroad.
•
Students will be able to follow order of events.
•
Students will be able to identify the pieces of advice on international opportunities.
Pronunciation
•
Students will be able to produce stress of multi-syllabic words.
Speaking
•
Students will be able to ask for and give information about educational programmes such as Erasmus, Jean Monnet.
•
Students will be able to present the information about international volunteering programmes such as Overseas Volunteers after searching on the Net.
•
Students will be able to talk about what kind of qualifications they need to contribute to their career.
•
Students will be able to express possible opportunities in different areas such as scholarship, internship, graduate study.
•
Reading
Students will be able to match headings with the paragraphs.
•
Students will be able to scan a text in order to find out the detailed information.
•
Students will be able to ask questions about opportunities abroad in the text or questions about studying the text.
•
Writing
Students will be able to write an outline for the essay.
•
Students will be able to write an application letter by using appropriate format rules.

EK_ALANLAR.Öğretim Teknikleri:
An eclectic approach to language teaching and learning forms the foundation. Teaching methods and techniques are selected according to the learning objectives and learners' needs and/or profiles.
•
Simulating the natural process of first language acquisition
•
Communicating in English in the classroom at all times
•
Constantly practicing real-life English in various contexts
•
Using a variety of interaction types (individual work, pair work, group work, whole class) during the lessons
•
Addressing functions and four skills of language in an integrated way
•
Focusing on “how?” and “why?” rather than “what?”
•
Encouraging collaboration among students more than competition
•
Fostering learner autonomy
•
Providing blended-learning environment
•
Providing safe, collaborative, interactive, and communicative learning environment
•
Using tools that can foster language learning
•
Promoting experiential learning and learning-by-doing
•
Using audio materials in listening, movies or short documentaries
•
Presenting unfamiliar topics by building on what is familiar
•
Discovering meaning from context and/or given clues
•
Modelling the correct use of language
•
Praising and positive reinforcement
•
Nurturing the willingness and motivation for language learning
EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
Assessment is used to promote and check learning. Multiple assessment types and feedback sources should be incorporated into assessment to achieve variety to document students' achievements throughout the learning process. Learners are asked to show what they can do and produce rather than what they are able to recall or reproduce. Besides the traditional assessment tools such as multiple choice, true/false, and/or fill-in-the blanks, a variety of assessment tasks reflecting the dynamic, communicative, and interactive nature of language use in real-life should be used.
•
Evaluating the integration of all four language skills as well as the other components of language such as lexis, structure, and pronunciation via Tach Pack, pen-paper in class exams or E-portfolios
•
Assessing understanding, production, and use of analytical skills in English
•
Evaluating listening/speaking skills via Discussion Time
•
Designing communicative assessment tasks and assessing production
•
Use of tools such as portfolios, projects, and/or communicative activities
•
Reading a short passage on a current topic and/or listen to a short listening excerpt (or watch a short clip) and then writing a short argumentative paragraph to defend their ideas
•
Selecting a random real life situation from a list given by the teacher and acting it out in the form of a conversation in pairs or groups.
•
Involvement of multiple feedback providers for different assessment tasks (self, peer, teacher, computer-mediated, and/or parent evaluation
•
Reading a news article and writing a short review or letter to the editor
•
Reading authentic story/stories and writing a constructed response stating a point of view about the story and using illustrations from the story to support the point of view
•
Reading an informative report and filling in charts/graphs/forms to demonstrate understanding

Students will be able to express regrets and wishes in their life.

Students will be able to talk about difficulties that paralyzed people live in our country and solutions to their problems.
•

•
Students will be able to scan a real success story of a paralyzed person.
•
Students will be able to identify the information about paralympics to answer the questions.

Students will be able to identify lexis and jargon related to paralympics.
•
Students will be able to match the definitions with phrasal verbs in the text.
Writing
•
Students will be able to write an opinion essay on ways of making paralyzed people's life easier by synthesizing information about paralympics they get by using information technologies.
•
Students will be able to write a letter or a note on wishes, regrets.

An eclectic approach to language teaching and learning forms the foundation. Teaching methods and techniques are selected according to the learning objectives and learners' needs and/or profiles.

Simulating the natural process of first language acquisition
•
Communicating in English in the classroom at all times

Constantly practicing real-life English in various contexts

Using a variety of interaction types (individual work, pair work, group work, whole class) during the lessons
•
Addressing functions and four skills of language in an integrated way

Focusing on “how?” and “why?” rather than “what?”
•
Encouraging collaboration among students more than competition
•
Fostering learner autonomy
•
Providing blended-learning environment

Providing safe, collaborative, interactive, and communicative learning environment
•
Using tools that can foster language learning
•
Promoting experiential learning and learning-by-doing
•
Using audio materials in listening, movies or short documentaries
•
Presenting unfamiliar topics by building on what is familiar
•
Discovering meaning from context and/or given clues
•
Modelling the correct use of language
•
Praising and positive reinforcement
•
Nurturing the willingness and motivation for language learning

Assessment is used to promote and check learning. Multiple assessment types and feedback sources should be incorporated into assessment to achieve variety to document students' achievements throughout the learning process. Learners are asked to show what they can do and produce rather than what they are able to recall or reproduce. Besides the traditional assessment tools such as multiple choice, true/false, and/or fill-in-the blanks, a variety of assessment tasks reflecting the dynamic, communicative, and interactive nature of language use in real-life should be used.
•
Evaluating the integration of all four language skills as well as the other components of language such as lexis, structure, and pronunciation via Tach Pack, pen-paper in class exams or E-portfolios
•
Assessing understanding, production, and use of analytical skills in English
•
Evaluating listening/speaking skills via Discussion Time
•
Designing communicative assessment tasks and assessing production
•
Use of tools such as portfolios, projects, and/or communicative activities
•
Reading a short passage on a current topic and/or listen to a short listening excerpt (or watch a short clip) and then writing a short argumentative paragraph to defend their ideas
•
Selecting a random real life situation from a list given by the teacher and acting it out in the form of a conversation in pairs or groups.
•
Involvement of multiple feedback providers for different assessment tasks (self, peer, teacher, computer-mediated, and/or parent evaluation
•
Reading a news article and writing a short review or letter to the editor
•
Reading authentic story/stories and writing a constructed response stating a point of view about the story and using illustrations from the story to support the point of view
•
Reading an informative report and filling in charts/graphs/forms to demonstrate understanding
